newsitem.title: USA: CBOT December corn expires quietly at $2.70/bushel.
newsitem.headline: CBOT December corn expires quietly at $2.70/bushel.

text.p: The CBOT December corn futures contract expired quietly at 1201 CST/1801 GMT Thursday with the last trade registered at $2.70 per bushel, traders said.
December soymeal futures ended $5 per ton lower at $240.00 and soyoil was bid at 23.02 cent per lb, down 0.22 cents. December wheat expired at $4.03 per bushel, down one cent.

Traders and analysts had anticipated an explosive expiry in corn and soymeal but heavy deliveries posted Thursday against those contracts alleviated much of the concern. There had been no deliveries posted prior to Thursday.
In late dealings, Cargill Inc was said to be a buyer of December corn while Rosenthal Collins was a seller. Cargill also bear spread at least 155 lots of March/Dec corn at seven cents, traders said.
The Dec/March corn spread traded at 7-1/2 to eight cents per bushel, premium December, in late dealings.

December wheat futures rallied briefly in early dealings as Term Commodities bought a small amount in the thinly-traded market. Locals were said to be sellers. The Dec/March spread traded at four to eight cents per bushel, premium December.
Continental Grain was said to be a late seller of December soymeal. On the day, Smith Barney spread 150 lots Dec/Jan at $15, premium December, traders said.
In oats, the thinly traded December settled at $1.48-1/4 per bushel, down 2-1/4. Commission houses were said to be light sellers late while commercials were buyers.

December corn settled at $2.69-1/2 per bushel, down 1-3/4 cents, wheat settled at $4.03 per bushel, up one cent, soyoil settled at 23.08 per lb, down 0.16, and soymeal settled at $240.90 per ton, down $4.10.
